results.question: How do broken-promise rates change with the number of previously broken promises?
results.got: Broken-promise rates increase steadily with each previously broken promise. Customers with 0 prior broken promises have a 40.12% break rate, rising to 50.74% after 1 broken promise, 59.84% after 2, 68.62% after 3, and 73.43% after 4. Counts for 5 or more prior broken promises are very small (12 promises total). [table: 7 rows]
sql:
SELECT p.prior_broken_ptp_count AS prior_broken_promises, count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.ptp_status = 'broken') AS numerator, count(*) AS denominator, CAST(count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.ptp_status = 'broken') AS DOUBLE) / nullif(count(*), 0) AS value
FROM l2.promises_to_pay p LEFT JOIN l2.collections_cases c ON c.case_id = p.case_id LEFT JOIN l2.agents ag ON ag.agent_id = p.agent_id
WHERE CAST(p.ptp_due_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '1900-01-01' AND DATE '2999-12-31'
  AND p.ptp_status IN ('kept', 'partially_kept', 'broken')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, prior_broken_promises
LIMIT 51

interpretation: Metric: Broken promise rate (broken promises / resolved promises)
answer.answer_text: Broken-promise rates increase steadily with each previously broken promise. Customers with 0 prior broken promises have a 40.12% break rate, rising to 50.74% after 1 broken promise, 59.84% after 2, 68.62% after 3, and 73.43% after 4. Counts for 5 or more prior broken promises are very small (12 promises total).

interpretation: policy and procedure for handling customer notification of a consumer proposal
answer.answer_text: When a customer discloses that they have filed a consumer proposal, a statutory stay of proceedings applies. Under POL-COLL-001 §7.3, the agent must immediately stop all direct collection contact, record the outcome (code BKPT: Bankruptcy / proposal advised), and place the case on insolvency hold (insolvency_hold). answer.insight: Under bank policy POL-COLL-001 §7.3 and §5.4, all direct collection contact ceases from the filing date, and cases on insolvency hold are excluded from standard cure and roll-rate calculations.

results.question: In the randomised pilot, do agents certified for vulnerable customers achieve a higher 30-day cure rate on hardship cases?
results.got: No, agents certified for vulnerable customers do not achieve a higher 30-day cure rate on hardship cases in the randomised pilot. Certified agents recorded a 30-day cure rate of 4.91% (462 cures out of 9,400 cases), compared to 7.83% (591 cures out of 7,549 cases) for non-certified agents. [table: 2 rows]
sql: SELECT cah.certified_for_vulnerable_flag, COUNT(DISTINCT cc.case_id) AS total_cases, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cc.cure_flag = TRUE AND cc.days_to_cure <= 30 THEN cc.case_id END) AS cured_30d_cases, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN cc.cure_flag = TRUE AND cc.days_to_cure <= 30 THEN cc.case_id END) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT cc.case_id), 4) AS cure_rate_30d FROM l2.collections_cases AS cc JOIN l2.case_assignment_history AS cah ON cc.case_id = cah.case_id WHERE cc.hardship_flag = TRUE AND (cah.assignment_method = 'randomised_pilot' OR cc.assignment_method = 'random') GROUP BY cah.certified_for_vulnerable_flag LIMIT 51

answer.answer_text: No, agents certified for vulnerable customers do not achieve a higher 30-day cure rate on hardship cases in the randomised pilot. Certified agents recorded a 30-day cure rate of 4.91% (462 cures out of 9,400 cases), compared to 7.83% (591 cures out of 7,549 cases) for non-certified agents.

results.question: Of accounts that were 1-30 days past due at the end of March 2026, what share had rolled to a worse bucket by the end of June 2026, by product?
results.got: For accounts in the 1–30 DPD bucket as of March 31, 2026, student lines of credit showed the highest roll rate to a worse bucket by June 30, 2026 at 3.13% (2 of 64 accounts, note small sample size), followed by auto loans at 2.66% (91 of 3,426) and personal loans at 2.55% (126 of 4,939). Credit cards recorded a 1.66% roll rate (384 of 23,096 accounts), while mortgages rolled at 1.09% (26 of 2,375)
sql:
WITH snaps AS (
  SELECT (SELECT max(month_end_date) FROM l2.account_monthly_snapshot WHERE CAST(month_end_date AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-03-31') AS d0,
         (SELECT max(month_end_date) FROM l2.account_monthly_snapshot WHERE CAST(month_end_date AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-06-30') AS d1
),
held AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT unnest(account_ids) AS account_id FROM l2.collections_cases WHERE insolvency_hold_flag
)
SELECT a.product_type AS product, 
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], b.dpd_bucket)
                            > list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], a.dpd_bucket)) AS numerator,
       count(*) AS denominator,
       CAST(count(*) FILTER (WHERE list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], b.dpd_bucket)
                                 > list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], a.dpd_bucket)) AS DOUBLE)
         / nullif(count(*), 0) AS value
FROM snaps
JOIN l2.account_monthly_snapshot a ON a.month_end_date = snaps.d0
LEFT JOIN l2.account_monthly_snapshot b ON b.account_id = a.account_id AND b.month_end_date = snaps.d1
WHERE snaps.d1 > snaps.d0
  AND a.dpd_bucket IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT coalesce(a.write_off_flag, false)
  AND coalesce(a.account_status, '') <> 'charged_off'
  AND a.account_id NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM held WHERE account_id IS NOT NULL)
  AND a.dpd_bucket = '1-30'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, product
LIMIT 51

answer.answer_text: For accounts in the 1–30 DPD bucket as of March 31, 2026, student lines of credit showed the highest roll rate to a worse bucket by June 30, 2026 at 3.13% (2 of 64 accounts, note small sample size), followed by auto loans at 2.66% (91 of 3,426) and personal loans at 2.55% (126 of 4,939). Credit cards recorded a 1.66% roll rate (384 of 23,096 accounts), while mortgages rolled at 1.09% (26 of 2,375).
answer.insight: Among high-volume lending products, auto loans (2.66%) and personal loans (2.55%) saw significantly higher deterioration rates into worse delinquency buckets than credit cards (1.66%) and mortgages (1.09%).

answer.answer_text: Under POL-COLL-004 §4.2, when a customer discloses reduced hours or pay, the agent must first acknowledge the situation and record the hardship flag with the stated reason (reduced income). Before requesting any payment, the agent must offer at least one eligible hardship programme option (such as a 3-month reduced payment plan or reduced minimum payment) and must not ask for an amount the customer has stated they cannot afford.
answer.insight: Under POL-COLL-004 §4.3, hardship assistance programmes lasting 3 months or less do not require proof of income.

results.question: Among randomised cases, compare the promise-kept rate of the champion strategy with challenger_A and challenger_B.
results.got: Among randomised cases, the champion strategy has a promise-kept rate of 53.77%, compared to 53.67% for challenger_B and 53.56% for challenger_A. [table: 3 rows]
sql:
SELECT c.test_cell AS test_cell, count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.ptp_status = 'kept') AS numerator, count(*) AS denominator, CAST(count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.ptp_status = 'kept') AS DOUBLE) / nullif(count(*), 0) AS value
FROM l2.promises_to_pay p LEFT JOIN l2.collections_cases c ON c.case_id = p.case_id LEFT JOIN l2.agents ag ON ag.agent_id = p.agent_id
WHERE CAST(p.ptp_due_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '1900-01-01' AND DATE '2999-12-31'
  AND p.ptp_status IN ('kept', 'partially_kept', 'broken')
  AND c.assignment_method = 'random'
  AND c.test_cell IN ('champion', 'challenger_A', 'challenger_B')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, test_cell
LIMIT 51
